title: Garlic Mashed Potatoes
subtitle: Yukon Golds boiled with whole garlic cloves and mashed with warm milk and butter: smooth, rich and made for gravy
imageAlt: A white bowl of creamy mashed potatoes with a pool of melted butter on a navy napkin
servingsNote: a holiday side for two with plenty left for leftovers

beforeYouStart.text: Start the potatoes in cold, salted water so they cook evenly to the centre.
The garlic boils with the potatoes, so it turns mellow and sweet, not sharp.

items.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
items.note: peeled and cut in 5 cm chunks

steps.title: Into the pot
steps.text: Put the potatoes and garlic in a large pot, cover with cold water by 2–3 cm and add the salt.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Bring to a boil, then simmer 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides through the biggest chunk with no resistance.

steps.title: Warm the milk
steps.text: Meanwhile, warm the milk and butter in a small saucepan (or the microwave) until the butter melts.

steps.title: Drain and dry
steps.text: Drain well. Return the potatoes and garlic to the pot over low heat for 1 minute, shaking, to steam off the extra water.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Mash the potatoes and garlic until smooth, then stir in the warm milk and butter, the salt and pepper. Taste and add more salt if needed.

fixIt.fix: They were overworked (a blender or hand mixer does this). Use a masher or ricer and stir in the milk gently.
They weren't quite tender. Next time test the largest chunk; for now, mash over low heat with a splash more warm milk.
Steam them dry in the pot a minute longer before mashing, and use warm milk, not cold.
Salt the water well, and season at the end; potatoes need more salt than you'd think.

saleTip: Yukon Golds in 5 lb bags are often $3.99–4.99 at No Frills; russets work too and are usually cheaper.
swap: Russet potatoes: same method; they make fluffier, lighter mash. Add an extra 2 tbsp milk.
leftovers: Potato pancakes: mix 2 cups cold mash with an egg and 2 tbsp flour and fry in butter until golden. Or top a shepherd's pie.
doneness: A knife slides through the biggest chunk with no resistance before draining.
source: Based on tested mashed potato methods (Canadian Living, Serious Eats): Yukon Golds started in cold salted water, steamed dry and mashed with warm dairy.
prepAhead: Make up to 2 days ahead. Reheat covered at 180°C (350°F) 25–30 minutes, or on the stove over low with a splash of milk, stirring.
Keep warm up to 2 hours in a slow cooker on Low, stirring now and then.
reheat: On the stove over low with a splash of milk, stirring, or covered in the microwave 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot.

fancy.note: Extra-rich: sour cream folded in and browned butter on top.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: fold in the sour cream after the milk and butter.

addSteps.title: Brown butter
addSteps.text: Melt the extra butter in a small pan over medium and swirl 2–3 minutes, until nutty brown. Pour into a well in the mash just before serving.

plating: Swirl the top with the back of a spoon.
Brown butter poured into the dip.

why.0-0: Yukon Golds are naturally buttery and mash smooth without going gluey.
why.0-2: Salting the water seasons the potatoes all the way through.
why.1-0: Warm milk keeps the mash hot and absorbs evenly; cold milk makes it gummy.

funFact: Yukon Gold potatoes were bred in Canada, at the University of Guelph in Ontario, and released in 1980.
